clue.text: Steamboat Bill's last changes to thin-sliced food

indicators.note: the letters of the boat's name plus one more are changed into a new order
the last letter of the word Bill's is taken, its final S being the possessive

explanation.surface: A film title, Steamboat Bill, seems to be getting a final edit before a food item appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes L, the final letter of Bill (the 's is possessive). STEAMBOAT plus L, rearranged by 'changes', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp, very thin toast is named after the singer Nellie Melba and is a classic thin-sliced food.

clue.text: Professorial sinecure?

parts.note: a professor holds a chair, and a sinecure is a post needing little work, so a comfortable one

explanation.surface: A cushy academic post with no real duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable armchair is a pun on a professorship with no work: an undemanding academic chair.

clue.text: Reportedly the management is not interested

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: the board of directors is a company's management

explanation.surface: Staff complain that the company's management just doesn't care.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering tedium and lacking any interest is the adjective's meaning, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Still taken in by Round Table in Barking? Pretend not to notice

indicators.note: the word for still is taken inside the rearranged letters
barking is slang for mad, so the words are rearranged crazily

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'yet more'

explanation.surface: A meeting of the Round Table service club in Barking, east London, where something is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the London district but means mad: ROUND TABLE IN is anagrammed, with YET placed inside near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from Nelson putting his telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal, meaning deliberately overlook.

clue.text: Leader in Turkey's elected once more

parts.note: an aga was a military commander or chief in the Ottoman Turkish empire
in means elected, as when a party gets in

explanation.surface: A Turkish political leader has been re-elected.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second time is doing it once more, a straight synonym.

clue.text: What pirate radio DJ did above 25, or medium in 18 19 made a volte-face

definitions.text: What pirate radio DJ did above 25
definitions.meaning: pirate radio stations broadcast from ships, so the DJ played records on turntables above the ship's deck
a medium at a fake séance makes the tables move in table-turning
a volte-face is a complete reversal of position or fortune

explanation.surface: A broadcaster at sea and a fraudulent spiritualist both changed things around.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is DECK and 18 19 is ERSATZ SEANCE. Pirate radio was offshore, unlicensed broadcasting, as from 1960s ships off Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reversing a situation so the disadvantage falls on the other side: a sudden complete turnaround.

clue.text: This roll on table might be turning potentially

indicators.note: the clue says this answer placed on the word table makes the longer word, so the table part is removed from it

parts.note: something able to be rotated could potentially turn: rotatable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bread roll sitting on a table that might be spinning, perhaps at a séance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer itself: this word put on TABLE gives ROTATABLE, 'might be turning potentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll in the sense of a list of names is a roster of duties, a synonym.

clue.text: Tells stories about old Charlie and moves elsewhere

indicators.note: the storytelling word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: to relate is to tell or narrate a story
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone recounts tales of an old friend called Charlie who has moved house.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift home or business to a new place is to move elsewhere, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drier's by source of water when left out

parts.note: by and to both mean near or against, as in close by, close to

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from the well word

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A clothes dryer sits beside a well, set outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like the comparative of dry; it is a thing that dries. The 's is is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for rubbing yourself dry after washing is a drier in the sense of something that dries.

clue.text: Text says you certainly are a man of great interest

parts.note: in text-message spelling the letter U stands for you
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'
in text-message spelling the letter R stands for are

explanation.surface: A text message gushing that the recipient is a fascinating man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Text says' signals text-speak: U for you, R for are.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant rates is a man of great interest, playing on interest as money charged on loans.

clue.text: They follow streaming songs, both loud and soft included

indicators.note: the two words for loud and soft are said to be included within the songs word, so they go inside it

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
low means quiet or soft, as in a low voice

explanation.surface: Music streaming services, with songs both loud and soft in the playlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaming' is not about music: it is the flow of air along a streamlined shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Currents of air move along streamlined surfaces, so they follow the streaming of a shape such as a wing.

clue.text: Can cast set round broken radii? It's not a 21Dn fall

indicators.note: the first rearranged group is placed round the second, enclosing it
to cast something is to throw or shape it anew, so the three letters of the first word are rearranged
broken radii are pieces of the word scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something cast in metal is fitted around broken spokes of a wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin, but it is just fodder for 'cast'. 21 Down is BASIC, in the chemical sense of alkaline: acid is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic precipitation is the opposite of a basic (alkaline) shower, so it is not a basic fall from the sky.

clue.text: Temperature finally touches 90 — the Spanish sun shines

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Temperature

parts.note: XC is ninety in Roman numerals
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A weather report: the temperature reaches 90 degrees as the Spanish sun shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touches' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outstanding at something is to shine at it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Right place for playing organ with style?

indicators.note: the letters are put into play, moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking where best to put an organ, the instrument, for a stylish performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical, but this is a plant organ; the style is part of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This female reproductive part of a flower usually carries a style, the stalk leading up to the stigma.

clue.text: Drawing in pale red is Echo and head of Narcissus (back to front)

indicators.note: the group goes in, inside, the colour word

parts.note: pink is a pale red colour

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the group is brought forward ahead of the conjunction

parts.note: E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A painting of the myth in which Echo pines for Narcissus, done in pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' is the definition, not a container signal; 'in' does that job. 'is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing made with a nib and liquid ink is called by this name, so it is a type of drawing.

clue.text: Crazy about hot water container shortly making comeback — these maybe?

definitions.text: Crazy about hot water container shortly making comeback — these maybe?

indicators.note: the crazy word goes about, surrounding, the rest

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: making a comeback means the shortened barrel word comes back, read in reverse
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the barrel word is dropped

parts.note: a water butt is a large barrel for collecting rain

explanation.surface: Someone mad about hot-water vessels; the clue asks if these are what they mean.
explanation.walkthrough: A water butt is a British garden rain barrel. The whole clue doubles as the definition: what someone crazy about hot water containers might love.
explanation.definitionFit: Large baths are hot water containers, which is the whole clue's reading of what someone crazy might be about.

clue.text: This worker fellow makes complaint

indicators.note: this answer plus fellow makes the complaint word, so the fellow letter is taken away from it

parts.note: a beef is a complaint or grumble

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles about a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the answer itself: this plus F makes BEEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile females in a hive are called workers, so a worker is an example of this insect.

clue.text: Where dogs might get picked up by ears cruelly after getting hit by heartless type

definitions.text: Where dogs might get picked up

indicators.note: after places the rearranged ears behind the other pieces

parts.note: to bat is to hit, as with a bat

indicators.note: heartless removes the inner letters, keeping only the outside ones of type
cruelly treated, the letters of ears are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cruel scene: dogs lifted by their ears and struck by a heartless person.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs Home in south London is Britain's best-known rescue centre for stray dogs. 'getting' and 'by' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous London dogs' home there is where people go to collect, or adopt, a rescued dog.

clue.text: With regulation I should be going great guns

indicators.note: I should be going says the letter I leaves the regulation word

parts.note: an ordinance is a regulation or decree

explanation.surface: Someone eager to follow the rules says they should be off, doing great guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going great guns' looks like an idiom for doing well; 'great guns' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery, or heavy guns collectively, is what military supply calls this; great guns are large cannon.

clue.text: Substitute fed to tigers at zoo

indicators.note: the letters are fed to, tucked inside, the words tigers at zoo

explanation.surface: A zookeeper gives tigers a replacement food.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ersatz is an imitation or inferior replacement, so the word means substitute.

clue.text: Irish boy's coke not satisfactory — where to find some spirits?

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish boy's name

indicators.note: not says the satisfactory word is removed from coke

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: An Irish lad, unhappy with his cola, asks where to get a stronger drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests drink, but these are ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where a medium tries to contact the dead is a place to find spirits of the departed.

clue.text: Get out of a channel in reverse drive finally

indicators.note: in reverse means the channel name runs backwards

parts.note: Dave is a British TV channel showing comedy and entertainment

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word drive

explanation.surface: A driver reverses out of a canal or ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' looks like a waterway, but it is Dave, a UK television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape or dodge a duty is to get out of it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Take huge risks with head of army following serpent queen

indicators.note: following says the risk-taking word comes after the snake

parts.note: a boa is a large snake
to dice, as in dice with death, is to take huge risks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gambler leading an army behind a snake, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: BOADICEA, usually Boudicca now, was queen of the Iceni, who rose against Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the ancient British queen of the Iceni tribe who led a revolt against the Romans.

clue.text: A herb cut about root

indicators.note: cut means the end of the herb word is cut off

parts.note: basil is a herb
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A cook trims a herb around its root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root' looks like a plant part but is used as an adjective, as in root cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Root, as in a root problem, means fundamental or underlying, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: I am adult having to be in working order (a 15Dn say)

indicators.note: having simply adds the next piece after the others

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
A was the old British film certificate for adult audiences
go means functioning properly, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: An insect announces it is now grown up and fully functional.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 Down is BEE; an adult bee is an example of this.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the final adult stage of an insect, so a fully grown bee is one, as an example.

clue.text: Blur seen in hotel magazines after Margaret leaves with son

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: Margaret leaves means the short name departs from the word magazines

parts.note: Mag is a short form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A blurred photo appears in hotel magazines after Margaret leaves with her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagueness or lack of clarity is what a blur is, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Capital of Libya. India. The Road to York. Kent area. Only Connect?

indicators.note: a capital is an initial letter, so the first letter of Libya

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the A1 is the main road north from London to York, written here as A then I
SE, south-east, is the region of England containing Kent

explanation.surface: Clues from the TV quiz Only Connect, where teams link seemingly unrelated items.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Connect is a BBC puzzle quiz; Kent is a county in south-east England. 'Only' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a go-between and keep contact between groups is to connect them, a close synonym.

clue.text: By end of year Kelvin's put up holly etc

parts.note: Dec, short for December, is the last month of the year
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: By late December, Kelvin has put up his Christmas decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn with festive greenery, as in the carol 'Deck the halls with boughs of holly', is a synonym.

clue.text: Company backing electronics firm turned local area network on and off

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the company letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Casio is a Japanese electronics firm known for calculators and watches

indicators.note: turned means the network letters are turned round to run the other way

explanation.surface: A company supports an electronics maker that switched its office network on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' looks like switching, but it is the definition, meaning now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens on and off happens now and then, intermittently, which is the adjective's sense.
